prior_importants.description: A merged session's open PR is never checked, because the gate deletes that session's local `refs/heads/pup/<id>` when it merges. The ADR check reads only that ref, finds nothing, and drops the peer without a note. The duplicate-number PRs this decision exists to stop still get through.

An `adr-number` refusal is reported as a flagged-debt refusal. The CLI prints "Merge refused:  flagged. Re-run with --accept-debt …" and the `pup status` inbox / conductor show "gate refused on flagged debt" with an `--accept-debt` command. Neither fixes the clash, because the ADR stage runs before debt is measured.

findings.description: `Competitor.pinned` exists only so `adrNumberStage` can patch `let theirs` afterwards with "its open PR's gated commit is not in this repo". That splits one decision across `competingBranches`, the interface and two statements in the loop, and one variable ends up holding either a reason or a result. Resolving the missing-commit reason where the pinned sha is chosen, or passing it into `peerDecisions`, would remove the `pinned` field, its JSDoc and the reassignment, and leave the loop as a single `const theirs = …`.

ADR 0146 (and the `competingBranches` JSDoc) says a passing gate deletes the session's local branch in both modes and only `pup fix` restores it. `gateAndMerge` keeps the branch when it had to keep the worktree, or when the branch has moved past the gated sha (merge-gate.service.ts L2023-2027). Reading at the pinned sha is still right in those cases, but a reader is told no such branch can exist. Saying "normally deletes" would make it accurate.

process_issues.description: The skill roster has review-simplicity and review-guards, but the record schema's area enum has neither. In this record, simplicity is recorded as `maintainability` (that reviewer's nit included) and guards as a second `conventions` entry. The schema in tools/review needs the new areas.

Skipped review-context (no CI/infra/protocol surface in the delta), review-workflow-safety (no .github/workflows change), review-maintainability proper (off the default roster; delta is 105 lines) and review-spec (no closing issue or --spec).

Deduplicated inline rather than spawning review-consolidator: the reviewers returned no important findings and only three nits, two of which (simplicity: the `pinned` field and the `let theirs` patch) share one root cause and were merged.
